newsitem.title: MEXICO: RESEARCH ALERT - Serfin started as sell.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Serfin started as sell.

text.p: Caspian Securities said Friday it initiated coverage of Mexican financial company Grupo Financiero Serfin with a sell rating.

"Grupo Financiero Serfin will be concluding its capitalization program in the next two quarters and should be able to turn around its large losses into a sustainable but low level of profitability in 1997-1998. Nevertheless, the recovery will be gradual, and the ADR does not deserve the unusually high valuation at which it is trading at this time," Caspian said.
Caspian said its opinion was that although fully reserved, the bank's price to book value of 1.8 times is expensive relative to the bank's profitability in the next three years.

Also, the price to book value multiple is also at unjustifiable premiums of eight percent and 30 percent to Banacci and Bancomer respectively, Mexico's first and second largest banks. "Further dilution expected in 1997 should negatively affect minority shareholders," Caspian said.

"Serfin should recover gradually, but profitability will remain depressed and constrain the bank's capital growth as the bank strives to clean up its balance sheet, rebuild its funding base and redefine its strategy in the next three years.

"Besides the ubiquitous asset quality problems experienced by all Mexican banks, Serfin will also continue to be plagued by its expensive funding structure, which will continue to put pressure on the bank's net interest margin," Caspian said.
